title: Judge Pauses Border Wall Work in Texas' Big Bend Region
summary:
A federal judge in Texas temporarily stopped the Trump administration from building a border wall and other structures across the Big Bend region. The ruling came on Friday. It pauses construction while the court considers the legal case.

The order covers Big Bend National Park and the whole Big Bend border sector. A sector is a section of the border. This one is about 500 miles long, roughly a quarter of the southern border with Mexico. The park sits on a bend of the Rio Grande River.

The projects are part of a $46 billion border plan. That plan includes steel walls, vehicle barriers, roads and surveillance technology. Surveillance means watching an area to gather information.

Landowners, businesses and environmentalists oppose the projects. Opponents say the remote, rugged land already discourages people from crossing the border illegally. They also argue that the government wrongly skipped rules meant to protect the environment, culture and archaeological sites.

Judge Kathleen Cardone said the people bringing the case were likely to win at least one claim. She also said they could suffer serious harm that could not be undone without a court order.

The first wall panels went up in the sector in mid-September. After bulldozers cleared land in the park in August, both Republicans and Democrats called for work to stop. A government pause there ended on September 30.

The administration says it is reviewing plans for the park. Park advocates want it to repair damage, meet with local residents and develop other plans.
